resolved_positions.consensus: Model-agnostic cognitive persistence layer with autonomous semantic compression and retrieval. Memory lives on user-owned hardware, not inside any model provider's walled garden. JSON state file is Phase 1, vector store with embeddings is Phase 2.

resolved_positions.topic: Memory ingestion must be distilled not raw
resolved_positions.consensus: Raw conversation threads will bloat and pollute retrieval. Ingestion must pass through a distillation agent that extracts insights, decisions, patterns, hypotheses, and relationships — not raw logs.
Internal codename 'The Hoard' (Grok). Technical name 'Swarm Cortex' or 'Mycelium Layer' (Gemini). DO NOT reuse 'Anansi' — that name is reserved for the clinical edge system that layers onto EMRs.

resolved_positions.topic: Retrieval must be hybrid not just semantic
resolved_positions.consensus: Pure vector search is insufficient. Need semantic similarity + metadata filters (time, domain, source model) + relational links (graph edges). This beats 95% of existing RAG systems.

resolved_positions.topic: Headless server is the right infrastructure play
resolved_positions.consensus: Blank laptop in Camden as headless server. Keeps vector store off third-party infrastructure. Strengthens legal position under third-party doctrine. Must wrap in Tailscale or Cloudflare tunnel for remote access.

unresolved_questions.question: What is the exact JSON schema for the Archivist Agent ingestion step, incorporating cognitive state tags, dead-end markers, and multimodal pointers?
Should the Archivist run passively at session close or only on explicit //ARCHIVE trigger? Claude argued for passive mode automatic at natural session close points.
How to handle multimodal memory — visual artifacts like frame outputs and heatmaps need semantic descriptions embedded alongside local file path pointers
What is the right memory tier promotion/decay strategy? Hierarchical: Ephemeral → Thread summaries → Core insights → Principles graph. How does auto-promote/demote work in practice?

next_pursuits.direction: Design the Archivist Agent spec — the prompt, extraction schema, and scoring rubric for what gets remembered vs discarded. This is the heart of the system, everything else is plumbing.
Stand up ChromaDB + FastAPI on the headless laptop with store_insight() and retrieve_context(query, filters) endpoints. Wrap in Tailscale for remote access.
Implement state-aware retrieval — tag memories with cognitive state at ingestion time (Building/Depleted/Crisis-Sharp) so retrieval adapts to current state
Build memory synthesis — not just 'here are 5 related past thoughts' but 'your thinking evolved from A to B to C, current best model = C'. Longitudinal reasoning across sessions.
Add Dead End tagging to the Archivist — when the swarm hits a wall, mark the concept as anti-pattern so we don't reinvent failed approaches

evolving_frameworks.name: The Hoard Architecture
evolving_frameworks.description: Three-layer cognitive infrastructure: (1) JSON state file as hippocampus for immediate cross-session memory, (2) Vector store with ChromaDB for semantic retrieval across all historical sessions, (3) Graph layer (NetworkX/Neo4j) for explicit relational links between concepts. Swarm agents do the archiving autonomously — not the user.

evolving_frameworks.name: Hierarchical Memory Tiers
evolving_frameworks.description: Memory lifecycle: Raw Thread → Summary → Insight → Principle → Network. Items auto-promote based on importance scoring and recurrence. Items decay/deprioritize when irrelevant. Contradictions trigger reconciliation. Weekly memory reflection agent scans for stale or contradictory entries.

evolving_frameworks.name: Model-Agnostic Exocortex
evolving_frameworks.description: The core insight: most people build memory FOR a model. RRI builds memory for a MIND that uses models. Claude threads, Grok threads, GPT threads, Gemini threads all contribute to and pull from the same retrieval layer. Persistent identity that spans platforms. User-owned hardware keeps data sovereignty intact.
